findings.evidence: T1 makes the wrapper create <root>\<runId> and <root>\uv-cache for EVERY actual launch, defaulting to %LOCALAPPDATA%\codex-sandbox-tmp. Existing suites drive the real wrapper with the fake and never set APEX_SANDBOX_TEMP_ROOT: dispatch-test, dispatch-preflight-test, dispatch-author-test, engine-dispatch-test, engine-test, apex-drain-test and others (each uses -CodexExecutable powershell.exe). None are in Files to Change.
findings.summary: Every existing wave and verify-fence run now writes to real host state (root, uv-cache, and a retained run dir on any non-0 final). Inside a Codex sandbox where LOCALAPPDATA is unwritable, the new mkdir would fail those suites. The spec also gives no failure policy for mkdir or a null LOCALAPPDATA. Fix: state that directory-creation failure is handled by the existing launch-setup catch (ledger failed, exit 1) and say how the existing suites are isolated (set APEX_SANDBOX_TEMP_ROOT in each, and list them in Files to Change) or explicitly accept the host writes.

findings.evidence: The spec says only 'in the existing pre-launch preflight path'. codex-dispatch.ps1:3199 opens `if ($Phase -eq 'build' -and $Sandbox -eq 'workspace-write')`, which contains the 76 gate, a -SkipBaselineCheck branch at 3245 and many 72 exits at 3260-3351. The lease is already open at 3141, before this point, and the dispatch reservation is at ~3633. $runId (2896) is available before all of these.
findings.summary: Without a named anchor the gate can land inside the `else` of -SkipBaselineCheck, which contradicts 'do not tie to the baseline bypass', or after the reservation. Also 'before reserving the dispatch' is imprecise: the lease already exists, and Exit-Dispatch 72 closes it through the outer finally backstop (4480-4484), so the 72 path itself is sound. Fix: name the anchor, for example immediately after the 3199 block closes and before the reservation lock at 3594, and require an unconditional check there on Sandbox/CodexExecutable/FORCE_CHECK.

findings.evidence: Exit-Dispatch (codex-dispatch.ps1:1010-1108) sets $script:pendingExitCode (initial 'unknown', line 89) and then calls `exit $Code` at 1107, so it never returns to a caller. The only hook that runs after every exit is the outer `finally` at 4476, which already reads $script:pendingExitCode (4484). The spec says only 'the wrapper's final teardown'.
findings.summary: The single final-result authority exists, but the spec does not say to hook the cleanup in the outer finally at 4476. Hooking after the inner `Exit-Dispatch 0` at 4463 is unreachable, and hooking in the inner finally (4470) runs before the code is final. Fix: state 'in the outer finally (~4476) when [string]$script:pendingExitCode -ceq "0" and the run dir was created by this invocation', and initialise the created-dir flag/path before the outer try so early exits do not hit an unset variable.

findings.evidence: The suite must run under the coder's own sandbox ('Coder verification: powershell.exe -NoProfile -File ...dispatch-sandbox-temp-test.ps1'), but the 'test-owned temporary area' location is unspecified. The bug being fixed is that inherited %TEMP% is unwritable in the Windows workspace-write sandbox. Fixtures also include git repos, the ACL fixture and a self-generated fake.
findings.summary: If the suite builds its area under $env:TEMP it fails inside the very sandbox this spec repairs, so T1's 'done when' may be unreachable by the coder. If it builds under the repo it trips scope. Fix: specify the area (for example under a writable root that is outside every fixture worktree) or state that the coder's run of the suite is advisory and HOST re-runs it natively. Also require APEX_SANDBOX_TEMP_ROOT to be outside every fixture worktree, so scope and tree-pin checks never see it.

findings.evidence: dispatch-test-fakecodex.ps1:108-205 shows the fake's final-0 path writes in-scope src/a.py, reports changed_files=['src/a.py'], and the blocked shape needs blocker plus not_run commands. Review-phase launches need -Schema review, a tree pin (3739-3742), and a verdict/findings report with no `status`.
findings.summary: 'Schema-valid report' and 'compatible valid report' are not enough to make the final-0 and final-67 cases deterministic. The self-generated fake must reproduce the in-scope write, a matching changed_files, and, for blocked, blocker, not_run and unresolved values. The read-only fake needs the review-shape report and -TreePinScript. Fix: name those requirements, or point at FAKE_CODEX_INSCOPE_ONLY/STATUS semantics as the model.

findings.evidence: 'whose FileSystemRights bitmask includes Modify or FullControl'.
findings.summary: 'Includes' is ambiguous between any-bit and all-bits. Modify is a composite value (it also carries Synchronize), so an any-bit test would accept a read-only ACE. An Allow ACE can also be overridden by a Deny ACE. Fix: specify `($rights -band [FileSystemRights]::Modify) -eq [FileSystemRights]::Modify`, and optionally ignore the root if a Deny ACE for the same identity exists.
